title: Cap. IX Arg. 6 Sol cont.: Corvinus's rule 'to him who does all he can by received grace, further grace is always given' does not shake absolute reprobation — no mortal ever does all he can
pass_a_gloss: Thirdly, That rule, Unto him that well uses grace (that is, as Corvinus expounds, pag. 157, unto him that does whatsoever by the grace conferred upon him he can do) further grace shall always be given, does not shake the absolute decree of reprobation. For I ask, Who of mortals has ever done or is about to do whatsoever by the grace conferred upon him he can do? The Angels did not; the first parents did not; finally none of the elect after grace of regeneration received does this; much less should we think any of the non-regenerate, furnished only with exciting grace, which Corvinus distinguishes from the living spark of nature, does it.
pass_b_english: Third: the rule To him who uses grace well (that is, as Corvinus expounds, p. 157, to him who does whatever he can by the grace conferred on him) further grace shall always be given does not shake the absolute decree of reprobation. Who among mortals has ever done, or will ever do, whatever he can by the grace given him? The angels did not; the first parents did not; none of the elect after receiving regenerating grace does it — still less any of the non-regenerate, armed only with exciting grace, which Corvinus distinguishes from the living spark of nature.
source_text: Tertio, Regula illa, Bene utenti gratia (hoc est, ut exponit Corvinus, pag. 157, facienti quodcunque per gratiam sibi collatam potest facere) dabitur semper gratia ulterior, absolutum decretum reprobationis non labefactat. Quaero enim, Quis mortalium unquam fecit aut facturus est quodcunque per gratiam sibi collatam potest facere? Non fecerunt Angeli; non fecerunt primi parentes; nemo denique electorum post gratiam regenerationis acceptam hoc facit; nedum ut facere id putemus ullum ex non-renatis gratia solummodo excitante instructum, quam a junce naturae vivae distinguit Corvinus.
